items.ja: ルイボスティー（アイス）
items.note: Caffeine-free herbal tea, naturally wheat-free and plant-based.

A well-known Nagano oyaki brand, named for the region's Jomon-era farmhouse roots. Dough is wheat- or wheat-buckwheat-blend based; filling (often nozawana greens, sometimes vegetable or meat) isn't specified here — ask which filling is on offer and whether it's vegan.
Deep-fried, panko-breaded croquette filled with Nagano beef and mashed potato — breadcrumbs and beef rule out both gf and vegan.

Deep-fried pounded rice cake wrapped in nori and typically brushed with soy sauce (the "isobe" style). The mochi itself is rice, but the soy-sauce glaze is the usual wheat risk, and the fryer may be shared with breaded items — ask.

items.ja: 信州りんご　シナノスイート
items.note: A crisp, low-acid apple cultivar bred in Nagano — naturally gluten-free and vegan whole fruit.

items.ja: 八幡屋磯五郎　七味唐辛子
items.note: The famous Zenkoji-district shichimi blend (see the Yawataya Isogoro shop entry), sold here as an add-on souvenir. Naturally wheat-free ingredients, but no allergen statement confirmed at this shop.

items.ja: プレミアム濃厚ミルク
items.note: Dairy soft-serve — naturally gluten-free, not vegan.
Nagano's grilled skewered pounded-rice cake with a sweet walnut- or sesame-miso glaze; the glaze is soy-sauce based and the miso may be barley — treat as containing wheat and not vegan by default.
A novelty-named fiery fried-chicken snack; fried and almost certainly soy-marinated and flour-dusted.
A cover charge, not a food item.

items.ja: 世界5大ウイスキー（スコッチ／アイリッシュ／ジャパニーズ／アメリカン／カナディアン）
items.en: The World's Five Great Whiskies — Scotch, Irish, Japanese, American, Canadian
items.note: All five styles typically use a malted-barley or wheat mash. Distillation removes most gluten protein by most food-safety accounts, but flavoring/coloring added after distillation can vary — a curious celiac should ask rather than assume safe. No animal ingredients in straight whiskey, so vegan.

items.ja: 軽食（信州牛コロッケ／フライドチキン／スパイシーチキン）
items.romaji: Keishoku (Shinshu-gyu Korokke / Furaido Chikin / Supaishii Chikin)
items.en: Bar Snacks — Shinshu Beef Croquette / Fried Chicken / Spicy Chicken
items.note: The same fried daytime snacks served as evening bar food alongside whiskey.

items.ja: 濃厚バニラソフトクリーム
items.note: Dairy soft-serve offered as a bar dessert.

items.ja: 軽食付きプラン（要予約・5名様まで）
items.note: A pre-booked (1 week ahead) tasting course for up to 5 guests; content and price are set to the guest's stated budget — no fixed menu is published, so ask the kitchen directly about every course.

Per a diner's Tabelog review, the night bar's compulsory otōshi starter is a daifuku (soft mochi stuffed with sweet anko) that guests may take home — the source of this shop's "daifuku and whiskey" nickname, though it isn't listed on the shop's own published menu. Sourced from a review, not the shop's own copy — treat as provisional. The rice-mochi wrapper is wheat-free; anko filling is usually vegan but confirm.

items.ja: モーニングセット　たまごのオープンサンド
items.romaji: Mooningu Setto — Tamago no Oopun Sando
items.note: One of two morning-set choices, open-faced egg salad on bread; standard wheat toast base.

items.ja: モーニングセット　カリッとバターはちみつトースト
items.romaji: Mooningu Setto — Karitto Bataa Hachimitsu Toosuto
items.en: Morning Set — Crispy Butter Honey Toast
items.note: Thick toast finished crisp with butter and honey — wheat and dairy.
Pressed, grilled sandwich — wheat bread; filling varies.
Curry-filled bread roll, oven-baked rather than fried, but still a wheat bun with roux-thickened curry filling.
Wheat-pastry apple pie, part of the kissaten-style dessert case.

items.ja: プリン（サンデーレトロプリン）
items.en: "Sunday Retro Pudding" — firm old-style custard pudding
items.note: The shop's signature dessert, made deliberately firm in the old-fashioned kissaten style — pick cinnamon or Yawataya Isogoro shichimi (Nagano chili spice blend) as a topping. Custard puddings are usually flour-free but not confirmed; egg and dairy rule out vegan regardless.

items.ja: 季節限定　珈琲ゼリー　はちみつ×ホイップ
items.romaji: Kisetsu Gentei — Koohii Zerii, Hachimitsu x Hoippu
items.en: Seasonal Coffee Jelly with Honey & Whipped Cream
items.note: House drip coffee set into jelly, topped with 100-year-old Omachi dairy Matsuda Milk's whipped cream and honey (red-bean topping also offered); the jelly itself is wheat-free, but whipped dairy cream and honey rule out vegan.

items.ja: 本日のストレートコーヒー
items.note: The house specialty — a daily-changing single-origin pour from a Tokyo roaster; one reviewer's tasting note compared it to aged whisky. Black coffee is wheat-free and plant-based.
Matcha whisked with steamed dairy milk — wheat-free, not vegan unless a plant-milk swap is confirmed.
Spiced black tea with milk — the spice mix isn't published so a trace-malt ingredient can't be ruled out; dairy-based regardless.
Caffeine-free herbal red tea, naturally wheat-free and plant-based.
Standard 二八 (nihachi) blend — 80% buckwheat, 20% wheat flour as a binder. Tsuyu is wheat soy sauce.

The house special: 十割 (jūwari), 100% buckwheat, grown on the Togakushi highland — one of Japan's three great soba regions, hand-formed into bocchi-mori: rinsed cold, gathered into small coiled bundles (bocchi), five bundles arranged on one woven zaru. Even fully buckwheat, it shares boiling water/boards with wheat noodles and the tsuyu is wheat soy sauce — never truly celiac-safe. Priced here as a 5-bocchi serving.
Soba with seasonal vegetables, likely in a hot dashi broth. Same wheat/cross-contamination caveats as any soba here.

items.en: Hot Soba with Matsushiro Mountain Yam
items.note: Hot broth soba topped with grated nagaimo mountain yam grown in Matsushiro, a Nagano-city district. Broth is dashi-based.
Soba topped with tempura — batter is wheat flour, on top of the soba's own wheat exposure.
Hot soba with duck and Japanese leek in the broth.
Soba with wild mushrooms foraged from Mt. Togakushi. Vegan status depends on whether the broth is kombu-mushroom only or the shop's usual bonito dashi — ask.

Buckwheat flour kneaded with hot water into a thick dumpling/paste — no wheat in the dumpling itself, unlike noodles. But it's typically dipped in the same wheat soy sauce tsuyu or a savory sauce, so ask what it's served with before calling it GF.
A fiercely pungent local daikon variety, grated as a soba condiment in place of (or alongside) wasabi — a Togakushi-soba signature. Likely just daikon plus a little soy sauce; ask.
Sticky grated yam, usually loosened with a little dashi and soy sauce — ask about the seasoning liquid.
Deep-fried mixed vegetable (and possibly seafood) fritter in wheat batter — not GF. Vegan status depends on whether shrimp is in the mix; not confirmed.
Miso paste grilled with whole buckwheat groats stirred in — a classic soba-shop nibble with sake. Miso can be barley-based (麦味噌); not confirmed here.
Japanese rolled omelette, usually sweetened with dashi stock mixed into the egg — check for soy sauce/wheat in the dashi. Contains egg either way.
Kamaboko fish cake, sliced and served with wasabi and soy sauce. Kamaboko commonly uses wheat starch as a binder, and it's fish — not GF, not vegan.
Tofu gently warmed in the starchy buckwheat cooking water, usually finished with a soy-based dip. Ask about the dipping sauce.
Chilled tofu topped with scallion, ginger and usually bonito flakes — assume bonito unless told otherwise (not vegan); soy sauce drizzle likely (ask for GF).
Shinshu's own speciality: thin-sliced raw horse, served with grated ginger/garlic and soy sauce for dipping — the soy sauce is the GF issue.
Raw horse liver, same soy-sauce dip as basashi.
House curry made with horse meat — wheat-thickened roux, meat-based.
Nagano-region beef, lightly seared outside and raw within, served with a soy-based dip.
Chef's choice sashimi, served with soy sauce.
Whole river char, grilled with just salt — no soy sauce or batter, genuinely wheat-free as a dish. Still confirm nothing else touched the grill, and it's fish, not vegan.
Mixed tempura platter, wheat batter throughout — not GF. Vegan depends on the day's mix (shrimp is common).

items.ja: 蕎麦の実とあんずアイス
items.note: Dairy ice cream studded with whole buckwheat groats and Nagano apricot (anzu) — the groats themselves are wheat-free, but confirm no other mix-ins; contains dairy, not vegan.

items.ja: 戸隠蕎麦と季節の料理コース
items.romaji: Togakushi Soba to Kisetsu no Ryōri Kōsu
items.section: コース / Course Menus (reserve 3 days ahead)
items.note: Multi-course chef's menu built around the house jūwari Togakushi soba plus seasonal small plates — expect the same wheat/dashi exposure as the rest of the menu across every course.

items.ja: 戸隠蕎麦と大将の特別料理コース
items.romaji: Togakushi Soba to Taishō no Tokubetsu Ryōri Kōsu
items.section: コース / Course Menus (reserve 3 days ahead)
items.note: The top-tier omakase course, chef's choice throughout, built around Togakushi soba — not GF or vegan-adaptable without extensive advance discussion.

items.en: Junsai Water Shield with Grated Mountain Yam
items.note: Junsai (a slippery aquatic plant, texture is the point per the ryokan's own copy) over grated tororo yam; likely dressed with soy-based sauce — ask. Note the location: Masuya is a ryokan in Yudanaka Onsen, Yamanouchi Town, about 22 km from Nagano City — this is a stay, not an evening out from the station.

items.ja: 旬菜色々（稚鮎の煮浸し、芋茎の辛子和え、ホッキ貝わさび和え、トマトもずく寄せ、杏）
items.en: Seasonal Appetizer Assortment — simmered baby ayu, mustard-dressed imokara stems, surf clam with wasabi, tomato-mozuku, apricot
items.note: A five-bite assortment including simmered young ayu river fish (soy-based nimono) and shellfish — not GF (soy sauce) and not vegan (fish/shellfish).

items.ja: 信州サーモン岩魚の昆布〆
items.en: Kombu-cured Shinshu Salmon and Iwana Char Sashimi
items.note: Two of Nagano's own farmed fish, Shinshu salmon and mountain-stream iwana char, cured with kombu; served with soy sauce for dipping unless requested otherwise.

items.ja: 志賀高原の清流で養殖されました鮎のひと口寿司
items.romaji: Shiga Kougen no Seiryuu de Youshoku Saremashita Ayu no Hitokuchi Sushi
items.en: Bite-size Sushi of Ayu Sweetfish Farmed in the Shiga Kogen Clear Streams
items.note: Sushi rice is seasoned with rice vinegar and usually sugar/mirin (mirin can contain wheat-derived alcohol) — not GF; fish-based, not vegan.

Served as a small in-course cleanser, not a full bowl. Whether it's 十割 (100% buckwheat) or blended is not stated, and the dipping tsuyu is standard wheat-soy-based regardless — never treat any soba course as GF. Vegan status depends on whether the tsuyu carries bonito dashi.
Thin-sliced local mountain char swished in broth at the table; broth base and dipping sauce not detailed — ask before assuming GF.

items.ja: 信州牛のサーロインステーキ
items.note: Branded Nagano beef; steak sauce may be soy/wheat-based — ask for tamari or a plain salt finish.

items.ja: 百合根白玉の蕎麦の実あんかけ
items.en: Lily-bulb Rice Dumplings with Buckwheat-groat Thickened Sauce
items.note: The ankake sauce is almost always wheat-starch or wheat-flour thickened even though the groats floating in it are buckwheat — do not read "蕎麦の実" as gluten-free.

items.ja: てんぷら（北信濃産アスパラ、山椒塩で）
items.en: Tempura of North-Shinano Asparagus, with Sansho Pepper Salt
items.note: Standard tempura batter is wheat flour — not GF. Sansho-salt dip (no soy) may make this the vegan-friendliest course if the batter itself is egg-free — ask.
Rice porridge with foraged sansai mountain greens; broth is very likely dashi-based (bonito) and possibly soy-seasoned — ask on both counts.

items.ja: 自家製トマトのシャーベット
items.note: Tomato sorbet — naturally wheat- and dairy-free as described; still worth a quick ask given the shared kitchen.

items.ja: 大岩魚のしゃぶしゃぶ
items.note: Same dish as the course-included iwana shabu-shabu but as a larger stand-alone order.

items.en: Shinshu Beef Steamed in Hot-spring Water
items.note: Local specialty technique — beef steamed using the ryokan's own onsen source water; seasoning/sauce not detailed.

items.en: Iwana Bone Sake (grilled fish warmed in hot sake)
items.section: 別注料理 (À la carte, drinks)
items.note: A whole grilled iwana steeped in hot sake — traditionally just fish and sake, so naturally wheat-free; not vegan.

sources: https://huuhu-gourmet.com/2025/08/25/長野駅から徒歩1分！人気「みそ家」のアクセス完/

items.note: The house bowl since 1959 and the only thing this 12-seat counter has ever served. Shinshu miso is a rice-koji (not barley) miso, aged for depth — sweeter and more aromatic than a Hokkaido-style miso ramen. Ordinary yellow wheat noodles, bean sprouts, one thick chashu slab. Wheat noodles and an undocumented tare mean this is not GF regardless of the miso itself.

items.ja: 味噌ちゃあしゅうめん
items.en: Shinshu Miso Ramen with Extra Chashu
items.note: Same miso bowl with four slices of pork chashu instead of one.
The miso base with seasoned ground meat stirred in for heat and texture.

items.ja: 辛味噌ちゃあしゅうめん
items.en: Spicy Miso Ramen with Extra Chashu
items.note: Spicy miso bowl with three extra chashu slices.

items.en: Miso Ramen with Stone-Milled Nagano-Wheat Noodles
items.note: Pay a small upcharge and the noodles switch to ones stone-milled from Nagano-grown wheat — thick, seriously chewy, and dark enough to look like soba in the bowl. It is the house's real reason for existing, but it is still wheat, just a different (and better) one; not a GF option.

items.en: Stone-Milled Noodle Ramen with Extra Chashu
items.note: Stone-milled noodle bowl with four chashu slices.

items.en: Spicy Miso Ramen with Stone-Milled Noodles
items.note: Spicy version with the stone-milled Nagano-wheat noodle.

items.ja: 石臼辛味噌ちゃあしゅう
items.en: Spicy Miso Ramen, Stone-Milled Noodles, Extra Chashu
items.note: The most-loaded bowl on the board: spicy miso, stone-milled noodle, three extra chashu slices.
Noodles served separately from a concentrated hot miso dipping broth — dunk and slurp. Same wheat noodle and undocumented tare as the ramen bowls.
Tsukemen with the stone-milled Nagano-wheat noodle upgrade.
More of the standard yellow wheat noodle in the same bowl.
Extra-portion surcharge specifically for the stone-milled Nagano-wheat noodle.
Fermented/seasoned bamboo shoots (menma) — usually soy-seasoned; confirm for soy/wheat and dashi.
Add three extra slices of the braised pork chashu to any bowl.
Plain boiled egg, not marinated — likely GF on its own, but confirm no seasoning brush; contains egg so not vegan.

Plain steamed rice — naturally wheat-free and animal-free on its own, and the only such thing in the building. Order it unseasoned, and be aware the counter, scoop and every surface around it belong to a wheat-noodle kitchen: survival food, not a safe meal.
Standard Japanese barley-malt beer — contains gluten.

The most-ordered bowl. Made with 安養寺みそ (Anyoji miso), a rice-koji miso from Saku aged over two years — far longer than an ordinary miso — for a dark, almost tannic depth rather than a bright salty hit. Seasoned pork mince is stirred through the whole bowl rather than laid on top. Medium-thick straight wheat noodles; not GF.
Loaded version of the house bowl — extra chashu and a seasoned egg on top of the pork-mince miso soup.

The kitchen's non-miso register: a Wakayama-produced tamari shoyu with a quiet sweetness, sliced chashu, menma, nori and a wedge of onion. Trap: Japanese tamari is brewed differently from Western wheat-free tamari and is NOT reliably gluten-free here — no such claim is made — and the noodles are wheat regardless.
Loaded tamari-shoyu bowl with extra thick-cut chashu, a marinated egg and greens.
Miso ramen enriched with a seafood (niboshi/dried-fish) stock behind it — a fishier, more savoury take on the house miso than the pork-mince version.

items.ja: 特製魚介味噌らぅめん
items.note: Loaded seafood-miso bowl with extra chashu and egg.
The lightest bowl on the board — a clear, golden chicken (Shiretoko-brand chicken) shio broth rather than miso, with sliced chicken chashu. Wheat noodles still apply; not GF.
A niboshi (dried sardine) stock layered into a pork-bone (tonkotsu) base — fishier and funkier than a plain tonkotsu bowl.

items.ja: 家系豚骨醤油らぅめん
items.note: A Yokohama Iekei-style bowl — thick chewy noodles, a creamy pork-bone-and-soy broth, nori, spinach and chashu. Wheat soy sauce and wheat noodles throughout.

items.ja: つけそば 濃厚知床鶏
items.note: Cold noodles dipped into a thick, concentrated hot chicken broth — Shiretoko-brand chicken.

items.ja: つけそば 魚介味噌
items.note: Cold noodles dipped into a thick seafood-miso broth.
Sliced braised pork over rice with scallion — the rice itself is GF but the chashu braise is typically soy-based; ask.

Pan-fried pork gyoza served with a Shinshu-miso dipping sauce; confirmed from the shop's mail-order lineup (sold as a home-delivery product), likely also offered in-store. Wheat gyoza wrapper — not GF.

Plain cold soba on a tray with dipping sauce. Buckwheat ratio (jūwari vs nihachi) is not published — assume a wheat-blended noodle. The tsuyu is wheat soy sauce based, and dashi is typically bonito — ask if a plant-based tsuyu exists (unlikely).

items.en: Cold Soba with Hot Duck Dipping Broth
items.note: Cold soba dipped into a hot, duck-fat-rich broth with sliced duck and leek — one of the shop's headline dishes. Wheat-blended noodles and wheat soy sauce broth; duck stock means it's not vegan either.
Cold soba plus a full tempura plate — wheat noodles, wheat-battered tempura, and a shared fryer stack three separate reasons this isn't GF.

Named for Togakushi, one of Japan's three great soba regions — served with grated daikon radish instead of a plain dipping sauce. Still a wheat-blended noodle and soy-based sauce underneath the radish.
The Iizuna-area cousin of Nagano's おしぼりうどん idea — a hot, sharply spicy grated-daikon-juice topping over soba. Not gluten-free for the same noodle/tsuyu reasons.
Plain hot soba in a bonito-dashi broth built on wheat soy sauce.
Hot soba topped with tempura — wheat noodles plus wheat-battered, shared-fryer tempura.

items.en: Hot Soba with Grated Mountain Yam
items.note: Hot soba with grated nagaimo yam stirred in for a slippery texture. Yam itself is GF; the noodle and tsuyu are not.

items.en: Hot Soba with Duck and Leek
items.note: Hot soba with sliced duck and leek in the broth — a classic pairing ("nanban" = with leek).
Hot soba loaded with a mix of mushrooms. Mushrooms are naturally GF/vegan-friendly but the noodle and dashi/tsuyu are not.

items.en: Grilled Dry Soba on a Board
items.note: The shop's own original — raw soba noodles grilled dry on a wire net and served with a scallion miso for dipping, no broth at all. Still wheat-blended noodle; the miso dip may be barley miso and its dashi content is unstated.
Sliced raw soba dough served like sashimi, dipped in the regular soba tsuyu — a novelty way to taste the noodle itself before cooking. Same wheat/soy caveats as the rest of the board.

items.ja: 馬刺し 赤身の最高峰 ヒレ
items.note: Raw horse sashimi (basashi), a genuine Nagano/Shinshu specialty, served with grated ginger/garlic and soy sauce. The meat itself is naturally GF; the dipping soy sauce is wheat-based — ask for a GF-safe soy or skip it.

items.ja: 馬刺し ヘルシー赤身
items.note: A leaner, lower-fat basashi cut. Same soy-dip caveat as the fillet version.
Tempura over rice with a sweet soy glaze — wheat batter, wheat sauce, shared fryer.
Tempura plate with rice, miso soup and pickles.
Boiled, salted soybeans in the pod — naturally GF and vegan; the safest order in the house alongside plain rice.
Chilled tofu with toppings (usually katsuobushi bonito flakes and soy sauce) — ask for a plain version without bonito or soy for a vegan/GF-friendlier bite.
Standard soy-marinated, flour-dusted fried chicken; not GF and not vegan.
Nagano's signature salt-pickled leaf-mustard, topped with bonito flakes here — not vegan because of the katsuobushi; confirm no soy/wheat seasoning for GF.

items.ja: 西之門 善光寺 純米吟醸 300ml
items.note: Local Nagano sake named for Zenkoji Temple — rice-based, naturally GF; some sake is fined with animal products, so ask if strict vegan matters.

items.ja: リンゴジュース 秋映
items.note: Single-variety apple juice from the Akibae cultivar, one of three Nagano-bred apple juices on the drinks list — naturally GF and vegan.

The cheapest item on the board and reportedly one of the least expensive station-platform sobas anywhere in Japan. Noodles are a wheat-blended machine noodle (not jūwari), and this counter runs soba and udon through the SAME boiling pot — cross-contamination either way. Broth is a fish-dashi, wheat-soy-sauce tsuyu, slightly stronger/darker in the Hokushin (north Nagano) style the shop says it preserves.
Same broth, same shared pot as the soba — the udon itself is 100% wheat.
Topped with a fritter (typically a kakiage-style tempura) — wheat batter on top of the wheat noodle and wheat-soy tsuyu.
A visiting blogger called this generously topped with mushrooms and seaweed for the price — good value, but still wheat-blend noodles and dashi tsuyu.
A raw egg cracked into the hot broth, named for its resemblance to a full moon. Contains egg — not vegan.
Topped with simmered sansai (foraged mountain vegetables — usually warabi/zenmai fern shoots). Vegetables themselves are plant-based but simmered in a soy-dashi seasoning — ask.
Topped with a sweet-simmered aburaage fried-tofu pouch, soy- and sugar-braised — confirm no bonito dashi in the braise for a vegan order.
The classic order at this stand — a fried shrimp tempura piece on top. Shellfish plus wheat batter plus wheat noodle.
Topped with rehydrated wakame seaweed — naturally plant-based on its own, but the broth beneath it is dashi/wheat-soy based.
One of the shop's two headline items alongside the tempura soba — sliced beef or pork simmered in a sweet-soy sauce over udon.

items.ja: 肉チートロそば・うどん
items.note: The stand's viral specialty — meat udon/soba with cheese melted in ("チートロ" blends チーズ cheese with とろける "melting"). It has been called out in "must-try station soba" rankings. Dairy plus wheat noodle plus wheat-soy broth.

items.ja: チートロスペシャルそば・うどん
items.note: The everything-bowl version: egg, a kakiage-style fritter, meat, cheese, onion and scallion all piled onto the wheat noodle base, with black pepper available on request.
A Japanese curry-roux broth over udon (soba can be substituted on request). Curry roux is wheat-thickened — not GF, and confirm no meat stock for vegan.

items.ja: 冷やしかけそば・うどん
items.note: Cold-broth summer version of the basic bowl, available seasonally.

items.ja: 冷やし山菜そば・うどん
items.note: Cold summer bowl topped with sansai mountain vegetables.
Add a second helping of noodles to the same bowl of broth. The shop notes this isn't always available if the broth is running low, since it's a fast-turnover platform counter.
Nagano's own fried chicken — a whole marinated thigh dusted in flour or potato starch and deep-fried; the marinade is wheat soy sauce and the coating is starch/flour, so not GF.

items.section: 信州マタギ鍋 / Matagi Hunter Hot Pots
items.note: One of the shop's 'matagi' (traditional mountain-hunter) hot pots — wild boar simmered with vegetables in a soy-based broth; genuinely unusual game outside Nagano's mountain districts.

items.section: 信州マタギ鍋 / Matagi Hunter Hot Pots
items.note: The most exotic of the shop's hunter hot pots — wild bear meat simmered in a savoury soy broth; a genuine Shinshu matagi (hunter) dish, not a novelty add-on.

items.section: 信州マタギ鍋 / Matagi Hunter Hot Pots
items.note: "Sakura" (cherry blossom) is the traditional Japanese euphemism for horse meat — the same Shinshu specialty behind raw basashi sashimi, but here simmered in a soy-miso broth alongside the shop's other matagi hunter hot pots rather than served raw. Priced in the same ¥4,389–5,390 band as the other nabe.
Raw deer meat sashimi, listed alongside the shop's Shinshu salmon as a regional specialty — the meat itself is naturally wheat-free but ask about the dipping sauce, which is normally wheat soy sauce.

Nagano farmhouse food — a wheat-or-buckwheat dough wrapper stuffed with salt-pickled nozawana leaf-mustard greens, then steamed; oyaki dough is wheat by default unless a shop states otherwise, so treat this as not GF.
Three different oyaki fillings on one plate — same wheat-dough caveat as the single nozawana oyaki; fillings vary and aren't itemised.

items.ja: 昔ながらの野沢菜漬け
items.note: The region's iconic leaf-mustard pickle, made the old way — plain salt-curing is naturally wheat-free; ask whether any dashi/bonito was used in the brine before calling it vegan.

items.en: Nozawana Pickle Over Rice in Green Tea Broth
items.note: Rice doused in hot green tea or dashi broth and topped with nozawana pickle — confirm whether the broth is plain tea or a bonito dashi.

One of Japan's three great soba styles — traditionally served in small bocchi-mori coils on a woven zaru basket. Even here, the tsuyu dipping sauce is regular wheat soy sauce and the same water/boards handle wheat udon, so never call soba GF.

items.en: Touji Soba (basket-dipped soba in hot broth)
items.note: A Hakuba/mountain-village style — a basket of soba is dipped into a simmering pot of vegetable-and-meat broth at the table, then the broth is drunk at the end. The broth itself is soy-seasoned, so not GF even if the noodles were jūwari.

items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: A rarity among Japanese pickles — Kiso-region turnip greens fermented with wild lactic bacteria and NO salt at all, unlike almost every other tsukemono; naturally wheat-free and plant-based as long as no soy sauce is added at plating.

items.ja: 信州そば粉の揚げだし豆腐
items.en: Fried Tofu Dusted in Buckwheat Flour, in Dashi Broth
items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: A local twist on agedashi tofu — coated in soba-ko (buckwheat flour) instead of the usual wheat starch, which is promising, but the dashi broth it sits in is bonito-based and usually seasoned with wheat soy sauce, so it isn't a safe GF/vegan bet without asking.

items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: Sobagaki is pure kneaded buckwheat paste with no wheat binder, grilled — the dumpling itself is the closest thing to GF soba on this menu, but the dipping sauce is standard wheat soy sauce, so ask before assuming it's safe.

items.ja: 信州ソーセージの盛り合わせ
items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: A plate of local sausages — commercial sausage casings and binders commonly include wheat, so treat as not GF unless confirmed otherwise.

items.section: 信州の食事 / Shinshu Rice Dishes
items.note: A Nagano-area katsudon variant — the panko-breaded cutlet is dipped in a savoury Worcester-style sauce over rice instead of the usual egg-and-dashi; wheat panko and wheat sauce both rule out GF.

items.section: 信州の食事 / Shinshu Rice Dishes
items.note: A regional specialty from Ina, southern Nagano — steamed wheat noodles stir-fried with lamb or mutton and cabbage in a soy-based sauce; despite the name it's unrelated to ramen broth. Wheat noodles and lamb rule out both GF and vegan.

items.ja: 北アルプスのおぼろ豆腐
items.en: Soft-Set "Oboro" Tofu, made with North Alps spring water
items.section: 長野の郷土料理 / Nagano Local Dishes
items.note: Freshly set, unpressed tofu made with mountain spring water — the tofu itself is naturally wheat-free and plant-based, but it's almost always served with a soy-sauce or ponzu dip, so ask before calling the whole dish safe.

items.ja: 信州福味鶏のやみつき揚げ
items.section: 信州の揚げ物 / Shinshu Fried Dishes
items.note: A branded Nagano chicken (Fukumidori) done as standard karaage — flour/starch-dusted and deep-fried, so not GF; the fryer is shared with other breaded items on this long menu.
Fried rice finished with fresh grated wasabi — the rice itself is fine, but fried rice at this kind of izakaya is normally seasoned with soy sauce, so ask before assuming GF or vegan.

items.en: Fresh Real Wasabi Root, grated to order (Azumino)
items.note: Whole fresh wasabi rhizome from Azumino, one of Japan's premier wasabi-growing valleys, hand-grated at the table — plain wasabi root is naturally wheat-free and plant-based; this is real wasabi, not the reconstituted horseradish paste served elsewhere.

items.section: 信州の家畜料理 / Shinshu Livestock Dishes
items.note: Shinshu-gyu beef simmered tableside in the classic sukiyaki sweet soy-and-mirin sauce (warishita) — the sauce is wheat soy sauce by default, so not GF.

items.ja: 信州蕎麦の蜂蜜アイス
items.note: Dairy ice cream flavoured with roasted buckwheat (sobacha) and honey — the buckwheat here is a flavouring stirred into a milk base, not a wheat-containing dessert, but it isn't confirmed additive-free; dairy rules out vegan regardless.

items.ja: 蔵出し原酒「大雪渓」正壱合
items.en: Unfiltered Sake Straight from the Cask — "Daisekkei" brand (1 gō)
items.section: 信州の地酒 / Nagano Local Sake
items.note: Sake is brewed from rice and naturally wheat-free; Daisekkei is a well-known brewery from Otari village at the foot of the Northern Alps.

items.ja: 長野全69蔵の地酒 全銘柄（精選）
items.romaji: Nagano Zen 69-gura no Jizake — Zen Meigara (Sensen)
items.en: "All Brands" Selection — one cup from any of Nagano's ~69 breweries
items.section: 信州の地酒 / Nagano Local Sake
items.note: The shop's headline conceit — a printed list running to roughly 70 Nagano breweries by name (真澄, 大信州, 佐久の花, 水尾, 岩清水, 七笑 and dozens more), any one poured for a flat price. Plain sake is rice-brewed and naturally GF/vegan.

items.ja: お造り（信州サーモン、馬刺し）
items.en: Sashimi Plate — Nagano Salmon & Horse Sashimi
items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: The course's raw course pairs farmed Shinshu salmon with basashi (raw horse meat), a genuine Nagano speciality served with grated ginger/garlic and soy — the meat and fish are naturally GF, but the soy dip on the side is not.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: Slow-braised pork belly and daikon radish in a soy-mirin simmering liquid — standard wheat soy sauce.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: Grilled skewers included in every banquet course — exact contents and glaze aren't published; ask whether it's a plain-salt or soy-glazed skewer.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: Standard wheat-battered, deep-fried tempura as a course course — not GF; ask what's inside for vegan.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: The shop's owner is from Togakushi and hand-cuts the noodles daily; even genuinely well-made soba is not GF — the tsuyu dipping sauce is regular wheat soy sauce and the noodles are typically wheat-blended unless stated jūwari.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: Whole river trout, simply salted and grilled — the main of the ¥4,700 course and one of the safest-looking dishes here for GF, since there's no sauce or breading.

items.section: 宴会コース / Banquet Course dish
items.note: Chef's choice of two sashimi in the ¥4,700 course; contents rotate. Ask about the soy dip for GF.

items.en: Cold Soba with Grated Mountain Yam
items.note: Cold soba topped with a raw egg and a side of grated tororo mountain yam — a visiting diner noted the yam arrives on its own plate. Not GF: wheat-blended soba plus wheat tsuyu dip.
A genuine Shinshu delicacy — field grasshoppers simmered sweet-savoury in soy sauce and sugar until glazed and crunchy; the sauce is wheat soy sauce.

The region's staple pickle — whole leaf-mustard leaves and stems salt-cured until sour and crunchy. Often plain salt, which would make it wheat-free and vegan, but many houses finish it with soy sauce or bonito flakes, so ask before assuming either.

items.ja: 信州鮭のハラスの塩焼き
items.note: Fatty salmon belly, simply salted and grilled with no sauce — one of the cleanest GF options here.
Whole river sweetfish, salt-grilled — one of the shop's own recommended dishes; naturally wheat-free.
Nagano's round eggplant, fried then soaked in a dashi-soy marinade — standard wheat soy sauce dashi.
A simple cold vegetable side; dressing not published — likely a soy or miso dressing, so ask.
Cold or grilled tofu topped with fuki-miso, a bittersweet mountain-vegetable miso paste — the miso base can be barley, so ask before calling this GF.
Whole small river loach, flour-dusted and deep-fried whole — a classic izakaya nibble but not GF.

The shop's roots — the owner is from Togakushi, one of Japan's three great soba-growing districts. Even authentic jūwari soba here is not GF: the tsuyu is wheat soy sauce and the boards/water are shared with wheat udon.

items.ja: 信州プレミアム牛ステーキ
items.note: One of the shop's headline items — a branded Nagano beef steak; ask whether the sauce is soy-based or a simple salt/pepper finish for GF.

Warmed sake poured over a whole grilled iwana (river char) skeleton and left to infuse — a distinctive Shinshu mountain-lodge drink; sake and fish bones are naturally wheat-free but obviously not vegan.
A genuine Shinshu mountain delicacy — wasp larvae simmered sweet-savoury in soy sauce and sugar until glossy; the sauce is wheat soy sauce.
A reviewer specifically called this pairing "exactly what Shinshu is about" — sake is rice-brewed and naturally GF/vegan.
Front-loaded appetizers, salmon/basashi sashimi, simmered pork belly, BBQ skewers, finished with hand-cut soba — no vegetarian substitution offered; treat the whole course as neither GF nor vegan.
The shop's recommended course — adds tempura to the 3,700-yen course's lineup; can swap to a winter hot pot on request. Same GF/vegan caveats apply throughout.
Built around a salt-grilled yamame trout main instead of the cheaper courses' pork-focused lineup; still finishes with soba and includes sashimi and tempura earlier in the course.
Slow-simmered offal in a miso-soy broth — classic izakaya starter, not GF.
Raw tuna is naturally wheat-free; the soy dipping sauce that comes with it is standard wheat soy sauce, so ask for it on the side or skip it.

items.en: Blackthroat Seaperch, Raw or Lightly Seared
items.note: A prized, very fatty Sea-of-Japan fish — the fish itself is GF, but the soy dip is not; ask for it served plain.
Fresh-cut live abalone — naturally wheat-free; the accompanying soy dip is not.
Plain raw sea urchin roe, sweet and briny, served without a sauce — one of the few genuinely wheat-free things on this menu, provided you skip the soy sauce that arrives with every sashimi order.
A rotating chef's-choice sashimi platter — the fish is GF, the shared soy dip is not.
Nigiri sushi rice is seasoned with rice vinegar (fine) but most nigiri toppings here get a soy-based glaze or come with a soy dip — not reliably GF.

items.ja: クリームチーズの信州味噌漬け
items.en: Cream Cheese Marinated in Shinshu Miso
items.note: A popular izakaya snack pairing dairy cream cheese with local rice-koji miso — miso can be barley-based, so ask; dairy rules out vegan regardless.

items.ja: もろきゅう　自家製にんにく味噌
items.en: Raw Cucumber Sticks with House Garlic Miso
items.note: Simple raw cucumber with a house-made garlic miso dip — depends on the miso's grain composition (rice vs barley); ask.
A light cold vegetable side; dressing not published.
Egg rolled with dashi stock — the dashi seasoning is normally wheat soy sauce, so treat as not GF.

items.ja: 九条ネギ入り京風だし巻き玉子
items.en: Kyoto-Style Dashi Omelette with Kujo Green Onion
items.note: A lighter, more delicately seasoned Kyoto-style version of dashimaki tamago — still built on wheat soy sauce dashi.

A genuine Shinshu specialty — thin-sliced raw horse meat served with grated ginger and garlic, dipped in soy sauce. The meat itself is naturally wheat-free; only the soy dip is the GF concern, so ask for it on the side.

items.en: Free-Range Chicken Grilled in Sweet White Miso
items.note: Chicken marinated in saikyo (sweet white) miso and grilled — miso can be barley-blended, so treat as not confirmed GF; not vegan regardless.
Spicy minced-pork tofu in doubanjiang-and-soy sauce, served bubbling in a hot stone bowl — wheat soy sauce base, contains meat.

items.ja: 信州プレミアム牛ステーキ　サーロイン200g
items.section: 信州プレミアム牛 / Nagano Premium Beef
items.note: A splurge branded-beef steak — ask whether it's served with a soy-based sauce or a simple salt finish, and whether the shared garlic rice side (below) is cooked separately.
Plain potato is naturally wheat-free, but this kitchen fries wheat-battered items (kakiage, karaage) in the same station, so cross-contact is likely; ask for a dedicated fryer if it matters.
Standard flour/starch-dusted, deep-fried chicken — not GF.
Toyama Bay white shrimp bound in a wheat-batter fritter and deep-fried — not GF.

items.section: 巻き物・寿司 / Sushi Rolls
items.note: Nori-wrapped sushi roll — the seaweed and rice are GF, but the nori is typically brushed with wheat soy sauce and the roll is often finished with a soy dip; treat as not GF unless confirmed.
Fried rice studded with chopped nozawana pickle, coloured dark by the soy-based seasoning — a nice Nagano touch on a standard chahan, but soy sauce rules out GF.

items.en: Rice in Green Tea Broth (nori / salmon / plum / mentaiko)
items.note: Choice of four toppings over rice in hot tea or dashi broth — plum (umeboshi) is the safest bet for both diets; salmon and mentaiko rule out vegan, and the broth base isn't confirmed dashi-free.
A simple wild-nori miso or clear soup — miso grain and dashi base aren't published, so ask.

items.en: Ice Cream (vanilla, matcha, or rum raisin)
items.note: Plain scoop ice cream in three flavours — naturally wheat-free; dairy rules out vegan.

items.section: 絶対に食べてもらいたい鯖 / The Mackerel You Must Try
items.note: The shop's headline dish, made from frozen-at-sea mackerel from Hachinohe, Aomori — the fish is lightly torched, but pressed sushi rice is typically seasoned with rice vinegar (fine) while the mackerel itself is often cured with soy or vinegar marinades; ask before assuming GF.

items.section: 絶対に食べてもらいたい鯖 / The Mackerel You Must Try
items.note: Fatty mackerel roasted over burning straw for a smoky char — no batter, so plausibly GF, but check the finishing sauce/ponzu.

items.ja: トロ鯖炙りしゃぶしゃぶ
items.section: 絶対に食べてもらいたい鯖 / The Mackerel You Must Try
items.note: Thin-sliced fatty mackerel briefly seared then dipped shabu-shabu-style — depends on the dipping sauce, usually ponzu or soy-based.

items.section: 絶対に食べてもらいたい鯖 / The Mackerel You Must Try
items.note: Classic vinegar-cured mackerel (shime-saba), lightly torched — vinegar curing is usually GF-friendly, but ask about any soy in the marinade.

items.section: 早すぎ御免 / "Too Fast, Sorry" (quick bites)
items.note: Miso-and-soy simmered offal, a standard izakaya fast starter — not GF.

items.section: 早すぎ御免 / "Too Fast, Sorry" (quick bites)
items.note: Raw fish minced with miso, ginger and green onion into a coarse tartare — miso can be barley-based, treat as not GF.

items.ja: いぶりがっこ酒盗チーズ
items.en: Smoked Pickled Daikon with Fermented Fish Guts & Cheese
items.section: 早すぎ御免 / "Too Fast, Sorry" (quick bites)
items.note: Iburigakko is Akita's smoke-dried pickled daikon; here paired with shuto (salted fermented bonito innards, itself a strong umami condiment) and cream cheese — no wheat expected but not confirmed; dairy and fish rule out vegan.
A local branded chicken, seared rather than fried — promising for GF if served with just salt, but ask about any tare glaze.

items.en: "My" Chicken Nanban (fried chicken in sweet vinegar sauce with tartar)
items.note: Deep-fried, flour-battered chicken in a sweet vinegar-soy glaze topped with tartar sauce — wheat batter and wheat soy sauce both rule out GF.
The salt-pickled Nagano leaf-mustard, battered in wheat and fried — not GF.

items.section: あて・揚げもん・鍋 / Snacks, Fried, Hot Pot
items.note: Egg rolled with dashi stock, seasoned with wheat soy sauce as standard.

items.section: あて・揚げもん・鍋 / Snacks, Fried, Hot Pot
items.note: Creamy potato salad served in a jar — mayonnaise-based; confirm no soy-sauce seasoning mixed in for GF, and it contains egg/dairy so not vegan.

items.section: あて・揚げもん・鍋 / Snacks, Fried, Hot Pot
items.note: A rotating plate of Japanese pickles, likely including nozawana — salt-only pickles are GF/vegan, but soy-marinated ones aren't; ask which are on the plate that day.

items.ja: ポテトフライ（七味山椒／カレー／焼きそば／塩こんぶ／のりしお）
items.en: Flavoured Fries (shichimi-sansho, curry, yakisoba, salted kelp, or nori-salt)
items.section: あて・揚げもん・鍋 / Snacks, Fried, Hot Pot
items.note: Plain-cut fries with a flavour-powder dusting — the "yakisoba" flavour powder almost certainly contains wheat; even the other flavours share a fryer with breaded items, so ask.

items.ja: 松代産　長芋の竜田揚げ
items.en: Matsushiro Mountain Yam, Soy-Marinated and Fried
items.section: あて・揚げもん・鍋 / Snacks, Fried, Hot Pot
items.note: Local mountain yam marinated in soy sauce then dusted in starch and fried tatsuta-age style — plant-based but the soy marinade and coating make it not GF.

items.section: あて・揚げもん・鍋 / Snacks, Fried, Hot Pot
items.note: Standard soy-marinated, flour/starch-dusted fried chicken — not GF.

items.ja: 信濃地鶏　塩つくね串
items.section: あて・揚げもん・鍋 / Snacks, Fried, Hot Pot
items.note: Ground chicken meatball skewers seasoned simply with salt rather than a soy tare — one of the more plausible GF grilled items here, though the meatball binder isn't confirmed starch-free.

items.ja: 長野とせったら　馬刺し
items.en: "Talk Nagano, Talk Basashi" — Raw Horse Sashimi
items.note: The shop's own tagline calls this THE Nagano dish — thin-sliced raw horse meat with grated ginger/garlic, dipped in soy sauce. The meat is naturally wheat-free; only the standard wheat soy dip is the GF caveat, so ask for it separately.
Raw minced horse meat dressed Korean-yukhoe style with sesame oil, soy sauce and a raw egg yolk — the seasoning sauce is wheat soy sauce, so not GF.

items.ja: これが長野名物！馬さし２種盛り
items.romaji: Kore ga Nagano Meibutsu! Basashi Ni-shu Mori
items.en: "This is Nagano's Famous Food!" — Basashi, Two Cuts
items.note: Two cuts of raw horse sashimi on one plate — likely lean akami and fatty tategami (mane fat), though the specific cuts aren't itemised; same soy-dip caveat as the shop's other basashi dishes.

items.ja: 昔ながらのチャーハン
items.note: Standard wok-fried rice seasoned with soy sauce — not GF.
Wheat noodles stir-fried in a Worcester-style sauce that itself contains wheat — doubly not GF.

items.ja: ご馳走おにぎり　映え。ねぎとろ＆イクラ
items.en: Loaded Rice Ball with Fatty Tuna & Salmon Roe
items.note: A rice ball piled with minced fatty tuna and salmon roe — likely finished with soy sauce for flavour; ask. Fish rules out vegan.
A standalone drink-only plan bookable any day — stick to straight shochu/sake/highballs to avoid sweet liqueurs that may not be confirmed GF/vegan.

items.ja: 特製胡麻さばコース（全10品・北信州地酒7種・2.5時間飲み放題付）
items.en: "Sesame Mackerel" Course — 10 dishes, 7 Kita-Shinshu sakes, 2.5-hr all-you-can-drink
items.note: The shop's headline banquet course, showcasing its mackerel dishes alongside a flight of seven northern-Nagano sakes — a good value way to taste the region's jizake, but the food course is not GF or vegan overall.

items.en: Portion sizes — large (+¥750) or small (−¥150), cold soba only
items.note: The single most useful fact about Kusabue: it is locally famous for enormous servings, and 大盛り (+¥750) is a genuinely huge mound, not a token extra — order it only if you mean it. Hot soba cannot be upsized.

items.en: Cold soba on a slatted tray, dipped in tsuyu

Even a 100%-buckwheat soba is not celiac-safe here: the tsuyu is normal wheat soy sauce and the same pot, water and flour-dusted boards handle wheat noodles.

items.en: Cold soba with shredded nori seaweed on top
items.note: Identical to mori-soba plus nori — the ¥10 difference is literally the seaweed. Even a 100%-buckwheat soba is not celiac-safe here: the tsuyu is normal wheat soy sauce and the same pot, water and flour-dusted boards handle wheat noodles.

items.en: Cold soba with grated mountain yam
items.note: Grated nagaimo yam, slippery and faintly sweet, stirred into the dipping tsuyu; usually loosened with raw egg and dashi, so ask before assuming it is vegan.

items.en: Cold soba with a sweet ground-walnut dipping sauce
items.note: The house signature and the reason to come: walnuts pounded to a paste and let down with soy-based tsuyu — sweet, thick and nutty rather than sharp. A Komoro and wider Shinshu tradition. Contains walnuts and wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Cold soba with a plate of vegetable tempura
items.note: Not served 15:00–17:00. Tempura is wheat batter from a shared fryer.

items.ja: 海老天ざる蕎麦 特上
items.en: Cold soba with premium prawn tempura
items.note: The top-of-menu plate; not served 15:00–17:00. Wheat batter, shared fryer.
Broth is katsuo/kombu dashi plus wheat soy sauce — not vegan, not gluten-free. Large portions are not available on hot dishes.

items.en: Hot soba topped with a mixed vegetable-and-shrimp tempura fritter
items.note: Kakiage is a loose patty of julienned vegetables bound in batter and deep-fried; it goes soggy in the broth on purpose. Not served 15:00–17:00.

items.en: Hot soba with grated mountain yam

Not served 15:00–17:00.

items.en: Mixed vegetable tempura fritter, on its own

items.en: An extra pot of the walnut dipping sauce

The regional pickle: whole nozawana leaves and stems brined in salt, sour and crunchy. Often plain salt (so vegan and wheat-free) but many houses finish it with soy sauce or bonito — worth asking. Served from 15:00.

items.en: Mushrooms dressed with grated daikon radish
items.note: Nagano grows most of Japan's enoki and shimeji; this is the cheap way to taste them. Usually finished with soy sauce. Served from 15:00.
